annotation.title_clean: My comments for 2021.IE26.12 – Commentary on Urban Robotics in Toronto (Automated Micro-Utility Devices)
annotation.title_en: My comments for 2021.IE26.12 – Commentary on Urban Robotics in Toronto (Automated Micro-Utility Devices)
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Orr, B. (The Municipal Infrastructure Group Ltd. / Urban Robotics Foundation)
named_instruments_referenced: Ontario Highway Traffic Act MUD pilot program
annotation.summary_en: Public comment from an engineering consultancy, prepared with the Urban Robotics Foundation, submitted to Toronto City Council. It opposes a proposed ban on sidewalk delivery robots (micro-utility devices). It argues for data-driven collaboration with operators, the Ontario provincial pilot and the developing ISO 4448 standard, and for accessibility safeguards.
key_provisions_or_claims: Urges Council to vote against banning automated micro-utility devices on sidewalks and cycle tracks.
Notes the Ontario MTO pilot under the Highway Traffic Act limits weight, width and speed and requires operator oversight.
Claims Tiny Mile robots covered 100,000+ km with no reported collisions, under human operator supervision.
Recommends collecting pedestrian data, geofencing, reviewing speed limits and pedestrian-yield rules, and accessibility training.
Cites the ISO 4448 standard under development by the Urban Robotics Foundation.
